technical.prompt: What is digital transformation?
expectedPoints: Using technology to change how a business works

choices.answer: Using technology to change how a firm works
distractors: Buying new laptops for all staff

technical.prompt: What goes into a technology business case?

choices.answer: Costs, benefits, risks, timeline and alternatives

technical.prompt: What is cloud migration?

choices.answer: Moving applications and data to a cloud provider
distractors: Moving the IT team to a new office

technical.prompt: What is the difference between lift-and-shift and re-architecting in cloud migration?

choices.answer: Moving systems as they are versus redesigning them
distractors: Redesigning systems versus moving them as is
Two names for exactly the same approach

technical.prompt: What factors decide whether to build or buy software?

choices.answer: Differentiation, cost, time, skills and vendor options
distractors: Only which option is cheapest upfront

technical.prompt: What is a data strategy?

choices.answer: A plan for how data will support the business's goals
distractors: A list of all spreadsheets in use
A policy for deleting old emails

technical.prompt: What is data governance?
expectedPoints: Rules for data quality, ownership, access

choices.answer: Rules on data ownership, quality and access
distractors: A government's archive of public data
A team that writes monthly reports

technical.prompt: Why do large technology projects often go over budget?

choices.answer: Scope creep and underestimated complexity

technical.prompt: What is scope creep?

choices.answer: Requirements growing beyond the original plan
distractors: A bug that slowly spreads in code

technical.prompt: What is the difference between agile and waterfall delivery?

choices.answer: Waterfall runs in sequence; agile in short cycles
distractors: Agile runs every phase in strict order
The two are the same delivery method
Waterfall releases new work every week

technical.prompt: Why are technology benefits often harder to measure than costs?

choices.answer: Benefits are often indirect and depend on adoption
distractors: Benefits are always easy to count

technical.prompt: What is technical debt?

choices.answer: The future cost of shortcuts and outdated systems
distractors: Debt owed by a tech company

technical.prompt: What is a legacy system?

choices.answer: Old, critical technology that's hard to change
distractors: A system inherited through a will

technical.prompt: What is software as a service?

choices.answer: Software run by a vendor and rented by subscription
distractors: Software bought once and installed locally

technical.prompt: Why does poor data quality matter to a business?

choices.answer: It leads to bad decisions and costly operational errors
distractors: It only matters for small firms

technical.prompt: What is process automation?

choices.answer: Using software to perform repetitive tasks
distractors: Hiring staff to do tasks faster

technical.prompt: Why is user adoption critical to a technology project's success?

choices.answer: Benefits only arrive if people actually use the system
distractors: Systems work whether used or not

technical.prompt: What is vendor lock-in?

choices.answer: Being stuck with one provider because switching is hard
distractors: A contract that locks office doors

technical.prompt: How is generative AI creating new consulting work?

choices.answer: Use cases, implementation, governance, workforce

technical.prompt: A $5 million system delivers $2 million of annual benefits and costs $0.5 million a year to run. What is its payback period, and its undiscounted five-year return on investment (net gain divided by the $5 million cost)?
expectedPoints: Five-year net benefit: $7.5M against a $5M cost
Net gain of $2.5M, so a 50% return

choices.answer: About 3.3 years; 50% over five years

technical.prompt: A project costs $3 million upfront and saves $1.2 million a year for four years, received at each year-end. At a 10% discount rate, what is its NPV?
expectedPoints: Positive NPV means the project adds value

choices.answer: About +$0.8 million

technical.prompt: On-premises IT costs $4 million a year; the cloud would cost $3 million a year plus $2 million to migrate. What is the payback?

choices.answer: About 2 years

technical.prompt: Building costs $2 million plus $0.4 million a year to maintain; buying costs $0.6 million a year. Over five years, which is cheaper?

choices.answer: Buying, at $3 million versus $4 million
distractors: They cost the same over five years

technical.prompt: 50 staff doing processing work cost $60,000 each, and 30% of their work can be automated. What is the potential saving?
A company spends $100,000 a month on on-demand cloud capacity. Reserving it cuts cost 40%. What is the annual saving?
2% of 1 million orders ship incorrectly because of bad data, costing $50 each to fix. What does poor data cost a year?

choices.answer: About $1 million

technical.prompt: A $10 million programme overruns by 45%, a typical figure for large IT projects. What is the final cost?

choices.answer: About $14.5 million

technical.prompt: A business case assumed full adoption, but only 60% of users adopt the system. What happens to benefits?

choices.answer: They fall to about 60% while costs stay similar
distractors: They fall to about 40% of plan

technical.prompt: 70% of a $50 million IT budget goes on maintaining existing systems. How much is left for change, and why does it matter?

choices.answer: $15 million, leaving little for innovation

technical.prompt: Why doesn't moving to the cloud always cut costs?

choices.answer: Poor optimisation and migration costs eat savings
distractors: The cloud is always the cheaper option
Cloud providers never charge for usage
Migrating systems costs nothing at all

technical.prompt: When should a company build its own software rather than buy it?

choices.answer: When it's a core differentiator with no suitable product
distractors: When a mature product already exists

technical.prompt: Why do transformation programmes need strong executive sponsorship?

choices.answer: Senior leaders settle cross-team conflicts and secure resources
distractors: Executives write most of the code

technical.prompt: What is the difference between a data warehouse and a data lake?

choices.answer: Warehouses hold curated data; lakes hold raw data
distractors: Lakes hold only curated, structured data
The two are exactly the same thing

technical.prompt: Why should a technology business case include a do-nothing option?

choices.answer: It sets a baseline and shows the cost of not acting
distractors: It is required only for small projects

technical.prompt: What are the risks of a big-bang system replacement?

choices.answer: Everything changes at once, so failure is costly
distractors: It is always the cheapest option

technical.prompt: Why should processes be redesigned before they are automated?

choices.answer: Automating a bad process just makes waste faster

technical.prompt: How can a company reduce vendor lock-in risk when moving to the cloud?

choices.answer: Portable designs, good contracts and exit plans
distractors: Moving all data to one provider
